_comment: Which assertions are decorative? This repo's flagship rule — a regression test must be proven to fail without its fix — is enforced by whoever remembers to stash the source. Three guards in one session turned out to pass against the code they were written to catch. Nobody has ever checked the other two thousand. Scoped to src/core because the pure engine IS the product, its tests are fast and deterministic, and mutating the Office.js renderer would mostly measure the fake rather than the code.
_comment_reporters: `json` added 2026-09-17 and it is the load-bearing one. The other three are character-for-character Stryker's own default, so the line used to add nothing while omitting the only reporter with machine-readable output — nothing to diff, nothing to key KNOWN_SURVIVORS against, no way to file an issue naming a mutant. It writes reports/mutation/mutation.json, which is the directory `actions/upload-artifact` already points at, so it costs one word and no new step. `clear-text` prints the per-file score table to STDOUT, which is NOT in reports/ and therefore dies with the runner; the workflow tees it to a file for that reason.
_comment_mutate: `scripts/round-pools.mjs` added 2026-09-29 — it is what `_comment_uncovered` below asked for by name. AND THIS ENTRY IS NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN: quality-sweep.yml runs `npx stryker run --mutate "$SCOPE"`, and a CLI --mutate REPLACES this array rather than intersecting with it, so the scope that actually applies comes from MUTATED and MUTATED_ROOTS in scripts/mutation-scope.mjs. Both were widened together and test/mutation-scope.test.ts pins them. Changing one and not the other buys a green run that mutates nothing, which is the exact failure the extraction existed to end.
_comment_dryRunTimeoutMinutes: Stryker's DEFAULT IS 5 MINUTES and this dry run needs 12. MEASURED 2026-09-13 on a 4-core box, once the earlier failures were cleared and it could finish at all: 'Initial test run succeeded. Ran 1803 tests in 12 minutes and 7 seconds'. On the GitHub runner it had been killed at exactly 5m00s with nothing but 'ERROR DryRunExecutor Initial test run timed out!'. This is a THIRD dial, separate from timeoutMS (which bounds one MUTANT) and from vitest's testTimeout in vitest.mutation.config.ts (which bounds one TEST), and it had been silently capping this job. The dry run instruments 43 files with 19,186 mutants and then runs the whole filtered suite once under perTest coverage, so twelve minutes is its honest cost rather than a symptom. 30 rather than 20: the measurement is from a developer box and a shared CI runner is routinely slower, so a 20 that is only 1.65x the local figure would be a cap set to fail on a bad afternoon — which is precisely the trap the 5 was.
_comment_ignoreStatic: Mutants in module-load-time code are skipped. Stryker cannot use per-test coverage for them, so each one re-runs the ENTIRE suite — a first run on five small files was still going after ten minutes for exactly that reason, and a weekly job that never finishes reports nothing. What is given up is mutating constant tables and top-level derived values, where a mutant either breaks everything (killed for free) or nothing anyone asserts (survives meaninglessly). The signal is in the functions, and they are all still mutated.
_comment_uncovered: WHAT WAS NOT MUTATED, WHAT THAT COST, AND WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT ON 2026-09-29. The pooled readers used to live in scripts/triage.mjs, outside `mutate`, and on 2026-08-23 FOUR tests written for them passed against the code they were written to catch — a reset test that a fresh module made vacuous, a batch fixture whose two entries never reached the case that differs, a confound fixture whose contaminating rows could not outvote a median, and a same-slide control that a filter dropped. Every one was found by stashing the source by hand, which is precisely the practice the comment above says nobody can be relied on to remember. The two blockers named here were both real and both are now gone. The 33 readers and the 12 declarations they need are scripts/round-pools.mjs, which imports nothing and reaches no filesystem — 2,431 lines out of a 6,655-line file, so `mutate` gains one small pure module rather than the whole tool. And test/triage.test.ts is no longer excluded: read block by block, only two of its describes genuinely could not run in the sandbox — a sweep that reads every file under src/, which Stryker rewrites by design, and a pair of 120-second child-process spawns that can never kill a mutant because a child does not inherit the active-mutant global. Those two are test/triage-repo.test.ts, which stays excluded, and its header records the division. WHAT IS STILL NOT MUTATED is the rest of triage.mjs, which reads the archive off disk, and `dormantInstruments` — the one pooled reader that reaches disk, through a default argument — which stayed behind with it.
